cluster_stories.title: China Will Open Its Market to AI Chips From US, Nvidia’s CEO Says
cluster_stories.summary: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, speaking days after he joined President Donald Trump’s summit in China, said he expects Chinese authorities will eventually allow the import of artificial intelligence chips from the US.
cluster_stories.headline: NVIDIA CEO: China Will Open Market to US AI Chips

cluster_stories.title: DeepSeek and China’s AI boom are increasingly powered by state money
cluster_stories.summary: Government-linked investors in China went from backing fewer than 10 AI deals annually before 2018 to more than 140 in 2025, reshaping who controls the future of AI.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA'S AI BOOM Now 70% STATE-FUNDED... DeepSeek Backed by Government

cluster_stories.title: Barclays Says Robots May Offset 60% of China’s Population Slump
cluster_stories.summary: China’s deployment of humanoid robots could offset as much as 60% of its projected decline in the labor force by 2035, according to Barclays Plc, helping sustain the world’s largest industrial base as the population shrinks at a pace not seen in decades.
cluster_stories.headline: BARCLAYS: China Robots Could Offset 60% of Population Decline by 2035

cluster_stories.title: China’s Energy Boom Could Give It the AI Edge
cluster_stories.summary: As the United States and China compete for dominance in artificial intelligence, energy is emerging as a critical battleground. Former Treasury Secretary Hank Paulson warns that while the US still leads in AI technology, electricity shortages could become a major constraint as data center demand surges. Former US Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns says China’s enormous investments in transmission, renewables, batteries, and power generation are already reshaping global supply chains, while Hoover Institution senior fellow Elizabeth Economy argues Beijing’s clean-energy strategy is as much about economic and geopolitical power as climate policy. Together, their assessments point to a growing reality: the AI race may depend not just on chips and software, but on generating enough power to sustain the technology. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: China's Energy Boom Could Give It AI EDGE Over US
